title: Structured matrix factorization length
summary: Every (resp. a generic) complex $n \times n$ matrix can be expressed as a product of $2n+5$ (resp. $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor +1$) Toeplitz matrices. Motivated by this result, it is natural to ask the following question: what is the minimum number of Toeplitz matrices required to factor a given matrix? We generalize this question from Toeplitz structure to more general structures. In this paper, we introduce the notion of structured matrix factorization length when the set of matrices with a given structure is an affine variety $X \subseteq \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$.
